I am 60 years old, I have farmed these 2 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. I only went to primary school. Everything I know I learned from doing it and watching my neighbors. My father farmed this same land before me.

My wheat is already in the field from last October. I used an improved wheat variety, the kind my neighbor Old Zhang used, about 25 jin of seed per mu. Before planting I ran the rotary tiller twice and put down one 50kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base fertilizer. Now it is spring and the wheat is shooting up. I top dress with half a bag of urea per mu — about 25kg — right when the wheat starts to grow fast. If you don't feed it then, the ears come out small. I irrigate three times: once at green-up, once when the heads come out, and once when the grain is filling. The well costs diesel but I have to do it. I spray twice for bugs and disease.

After I cut the wheat in early June, I plant maize the same day. I don't waste a single day. I use hybrid seed, about 4 jin per mu. I plant right into the wheat stubble without plowing — everyone does it now, saves time and diesel. I put down 40kg of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then when the maize is knee-high I spread another 25kg of urea per mu. Maize grows fast and needs its food then. I irrigate twice: once after planting if it is dry, and once when the plants are making ears. I spray twice for the corn borer worm — that worm can ruin the whole crop if you let it.

I don't calculate everything like an expert. I watch what the neighbors do. If Old Zhang puts half a bag of urea on his wheat, I do the same. Fertilizer is expensive — a bag of urea is over 100 yuan now — but I would rather put a bit too much than too little. If I lose yield, my family loses grain and money. A bad harvest is a disaster. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost. Last year my wheat made about 900 jin per mu and maize about 1000 jin per mu. I expect about the same this year if the weather holds. My son works in a factory in Handan and sends some money home, but these 2 mu still matter for our food and for selling.
